problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting packages to load onto a delivery truck. The available packages are:
* Package 1: size 30 cubic feet, revenue $95
* Package 2: size 3 cubic feet, revenue $95
* Package 3: size 42 cubic feet, revenue $14
* Package 4: size 34 cubic feet, revenue $214
* Package 5: size 23 cubic feet, revenue $56
* Package 6: size 21 cubic feet, revenue $23
* Package 7: size 44 cubic feet, revenue $246
* Package 8: size 47 cubic feet, revenue $270
* Package 9: size 15 cubic feet, revenue $142
* Package 10: size 25 cubic feet, revenue $40
* Package 11: size 28 cubic feet, revenue $240
* Package 12: size 32 cubic feet, revenue $94
* Package 13: size 14 cubic feet, revenue $66
* Package 14: size 35 cubic feet, revenue $274
* Package 15: size 7 cubic feet, revenue $278
* Package 16: size 14 cubic feet, revenue $296
* Package 17: size 26 cubic feet, revenue $174
* Package 18: size 18 cubic feet, revenue $128
* Package 19: size 48 cubic feet, revenue $40
* Package 20: size 21 cubic feet, revenue $152
* Package 21: size 6 cubic feet, revenue $104
* Package 22: size 7 cubic feet, revenue $245
* Package 23: size 50 cubic feet, revenue $21
* Package 24: size 31 cubic feet, revenue $191

The truck has a maximum cargo capacity of 434 cubic feet. Choose the combination of packages that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this capacity limit. Each package must be either fully accepted or rejected.
